sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code README.md
sources.locator: Current features; Setup; Session continuity; Monitoring; Roadmap
sources.finding: Ralph drives repeated Claude Code calls using local prompt/spec/task files. Product CLI commands, rate limits, circuit breakers, live output, session expiry, notifications and backup/rollback are documented.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code docs/CLI_OPTIONS.md
sources.finding: The CLI configures hourly calls, timeouts, tool allowlists, session resets and queue processing. Repository-controlled ALLOWED_TOOLS is explicitly not a security boundary.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code docs/QUEUE_MANAGEMENT.md
sources.finding: A persistent queue imports GitHub issues or local PRDs, tracks states and priorities, enforces in-queue dependencies, skips duplicate IDs and processes items sequentially on the current branch.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code docs/DOCKER_SANDBOX.md
sources.finding: Docker executes Claude inside a persistent container with a read-write project bind mount. Host orchestration remains local, CPU/memory/network are configurable, and credentials are scoped copies or API keys.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code docs/E2B_SANDBOX.md
sources.finding: E2B runs Claude remotely while the host loop controls iterations and file sync. Sandbox expiry can recreate/reupload; cost limits use estimates rather than invoices.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code docs/user-guide/02-understanding-ralph-files.md
sources.finding: User-editable prompt/spec files and prioritized checklists provide the loop context and work plan. They are files rather than a documented revision/approval system.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code docs/adr/0001-multi-provider-agent-abstraction.md
sources.finding: Multi-provider abstraction is a planning item. It does not establish released Codex, Gemini or OpenCode support.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code ralph_monitor.sh
sources.finding: The actual monitor reads local status/progress/queue JSON and log files, displays loop/API-call counts and queue state totals, and refreshes every two seconds.

sources.title: Ralph for Claude Code LICENSE
sources.finding: Ralph repository code is MIT licensed.

sources.title: ralph-claude-code README
sources.finding: Says the tool is MIT licensed. Claude auth can use your own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or Claude credentials. The optional E2B cloud sandbox has cost estimated from runtime times a user-set hourly rate, with budget caps, and E2B charges for it.

sources.title: frankbria/ralph-claude-code LICENSE (MIT)
sources.finding: The MIT License lets anyone obtain, use, copy and modify the software free of charge.

sources.title: Ralph README: GitHub issue lifecycle
sources.locator: README.md lines 518-550 (GitHub issue lifecycle flags), commit 11f9df5
sources.finding: With --github-issue, Ralph uses the gh CLI to post progress comments, create a pull request on completion (optionally as a draft and linked with Closes #N), post a summary, close the issue and open follow-up issues.

sources.title: Ralph README: how credentials reach the container
sources.locator: README.md lines 636-642, commit 11f9df5; default CLAUDE_CODE_CMD=claude at ralph_loop.sh line 124
sources.finding: On the host Ralph invokes the installed claude CLI (default command claude), which uses its own sign-in. In the Docker sandbox it passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when set, otherwise copies the user's ~/.claude/.credentials.json into a container-scoped home.

sources.title: Ralph README: installation
sources.finding: Ralph is installed globally from a clone of the public repository with ./install.sh; the README names no price, account or paid plan.
